title: High-Throughput Ancient DNA Extraction Method for Sample Screening
author: Alexandre Gilardet

steps.title: Lysis of bone fragments
steps.instruction: Add ~50 mg bone fragments or powder to a 2 mL screw‑cap tube, prepare 1000.5 µL lysis buffer (900 µL 0.5 M EDTA pH 8, 75 µL ultrapure water, 0.5 µL 10 % Tween‑20, 25 µL 10 µg/µL Proteinase K), mix by pipetting, incubate at 37 °C with rotation overnight (powder) or several days for fragments, add 20 µL extra Proteinase K after 48 h if needed, store lysates at –20 °C until extraction.

substeps.instruction: Add ~50 mg bone fragments or powder to a 2 mL screw‑cap tube.
Add 900 µL 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8), 75 µL ultrapure water, 0.5 µL Tween‑20 (10 %), and 25 µL Proteinase K (10 µg/µL) to make 1000.5 µL lysis buffer.
Mix by pipetting.
Incubate at 37 °C with rotation overnight for powder; for fragments, allow several days for dissolution.
If fragments are still not fully dissolved after 48 h, add an additional 20 µL Proteinase K.
Store lysates at –20 °C until extraction.

steps.title: Prepare binding buffer aliquots
steps.instruction: For 35 mL (~35 extractions) aliquot 1 mL binding buffer into 1.5 mL LoBind tubes, add 40 µL sodium acetate to each, UV‑decontaminate ultrapure water before buffer preparation and also UV‑decontaminate PE and elution buffer aliquots before extraction; sodium acetate may be added to the original binding‑buffer mix, but do not store the buffer after sodium acetate addition.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 1 mL binding buffer into each 1.5 mL LoBind tube (prepare enough for ~35 extractions).
Add 40 µL sodium acetate to each aliquot.
UV‑decontaminate ultrapure water before preparing the binding buffer.
UV‑decontaminate PE and elution buffer aliquots before starting extraction.
Note: sodium acetate can be added to the original binding‑buffer mix, but the mixed buffer should not be stored.

steps.title: Set up vacuum and check pressure
steps.instruction: Seal a new QIAquick 96‑well plate, place it on the QIAvac top plate above the waste tray, keep the plate on the top plate throughout, ensure a waste tray or collection rack is underneath, insert the set‑up into the QIAvac base, close the valve between pump and manifold, switch on the vacuum pump, let the needle stabilize, adjust control to < ‑800 mbar, open valve, let needle stabilize to < ‑600 mbar; if no pressure, check connections before proceeding.

substeps.instruction: Seal a new QIAquick 96‑well plate.
Place the sealed plate on the QIAvac top plate, above the waste tray.
Keep the plate on the top plate for the whole procedure; ensure waste tray or collection rack is underneath before pipetting.
Insert the assembly into the QIAvac base.
Close the valve between the vacuum pump/manifold.
Switch on the vacuum pump and allow the needle to stabilize.
If needed, lower the control to below –800 mbar.
Open the valve and let the needle stabilize again to below –600 mbar.
If pressure does not develop, check all connections before continuing.

steps.title: Mix lysate with binding buffer
steps.instruction: Let the lysate equilibrate to room temperature, vortex, centrifuge at 6000 g for 3 min, then combine 100 µL lysate aliquot with one binding‑buffer aliquot (containing sodium acetate), vortex vigorously; use an adjustable multichannel pipette for parallel processing.

substeps.instruction: Allow lysate to reach room temperature.
Vortex the lysate.
Centrifuge lysate at 6000 g for 3 min.
Transfer 100 µL lysate to a binding‑buffer aliquot (with sodium acetate).
Vortex the mixture vigorously.
Use an adjustable multichannel pipette to process multiple samples in parallel.

steps.title: Bind DNA to silica columns
steps.instruction: Remove the seal from the QIAquick 96‑well plate, pipette half of the lysate‑binding mixture onto each column (record plate layout), adapt plate, top plate and waste tray to the QIAvac base and turn on vacuum as in step 3, then add the remaining mixture (second load) due to column volume limits, and dispose of waste according to guanidine‑hydrochloride guidelines.

substeps.instruction: Remove the seal from the QIAquick 96‑well plate.
Pipette half of the lysate‑binding mixture onto each column using a multichannel pipette.
Record the sample layout on the plate.
Adapt the plate, top plate, and waste tray to the QIAvac base.
Turn on the vacuum following the procedure in step 3.
Add the remaining lysate‑binding mixture to the columns (second load) because of column volume limits.
Empty the waste tray following guanidine‑hydrochloride waste‑management procedures.

steps.title: Wash columns with PE buffer
steps.instruction: Apply 900 µL PE buffer to each column, turn on vacuum, repeat the wash once, then apply maximum vacuum for 10 min to remove all wash liquid, lift plate and top plate together, ventilate slowly and tap on absorbent paper until nozzles are dry.

substeps.instruction: Apply 900 µL PE buffer to each column.
Turn on vacuum to draw buffer through.
Repeat the 900 µL PE wash a second time.
Apply maximum vacuum to the plate for 10 min to eliminate residual wash buffer.
Lift the plate and top plate together.
Ventilate the assembly slowly.
Tap the plate on absorbent paper until the column nozzles are dry.

steps.title: Elute DNA from columns
steps.instruction: Transfer the plate and top plate from the waste tray to a collection rack, add 60 µL elution buffer (TET recommended) to each column, incubate at room temperature for 5 min, then apply vacuum for 5 min; annotate collection tubes according to the plate map.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the plate and top plate from the waste tray to a collection rack.
Add 60 µL elution buffer (TET) to each column.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Apply vacuum for 5 min to collect eluate.
Annotate the collection tubes according to the plate map.

steps.title: Prepare DNA library (optional)
steps.instruction: Prepare a DNA library from the extracted DNA according to the laboratory‑specific protocol.
